card.summary: H.R. 5371, the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, ends the government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. summary: S. 2256 is the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026. The bill provides federal funding and sets legal requirements and restrictions for the Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Farm Credit Administration, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026.

affected_groups.effect: Receive access to direct and guaranteed farm loans, crop insurance support, conservation technical assistance, and specific grants and indemnity programs.
Benefit from federal investments in rural housing loans, community facilities, water and waste disposal infrastructure, broadband deployment, and business development grants.
Participate in or receive benefits through domestic nutrition assistance programs, including SNAP, WIC, school meals, and commodity assistance.
Subject to FDA oversight, inspections, and regulatory standards funded by the legislation, including specific provisions on tobacco products, seafood imports, and labeling.
affected_groups.group: Food and medical product manufacturers and consumers

key_provisions: Provides discretionary and mandatory appropriations for USDA agricultural programs, research agencies, conservation operations, and farm production and conservation programs.

Allocates funding for USDA rural development programs, including housing loans, community facilities, rural business programs, and water and waste disposal systems, specifying that a portion of funds target persistent poverty counties.

Funds domestic food assistance programs, including child nutrition programs, the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
Provides appropriations for foreign assistance and related programs, including Food for Peace Title II grants and the McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program.
Funds the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), incorporating specific user fee collections for prescription drugs, medical devices, tobacco products, and other regulated items.

Imposes general provisions and restrictions, such as rules regarding the domestic sourcing of iron and steel for rural water and waste projects, oversight of agricultural land transactions involving foreign entities, and updates to the definition of hemp.
Rescinds specified unobligated balances from prior year appropriations across several accounts.

The bill provides federal funding and sets legal requirements and restrictions for the Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Farm Credit Administration, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026.
summary_detail.significance: The bill dictates federal spending and operational priorities for major agricultural, nutritional, and public health agencies, affecting federal funding levels and regulatory enforcement across the United States food and rural infrastructure sectors for fiscal year 2026.
